Hi Alyssa,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — great questions from your ML infra team. I wanted to follow up specifically on how we bill for prefix ("residency") cache hits vs. cold token generation so you have an answer for procurement. A couple of quick points and then a couple asks so we can give you a precise quote: 

- Short answer: when an incoming request reuses a cached prefix (exact match on prefix + model variant + temperature), we meter only the incremental tokens generated after the cache hit. In other words, full prompt tokens are not double-billed for that matched prefix.
- Edge cases to call out: partial prefix matches (e.g., slightly different system prompts) are treated as misses and billed for full prompt tokens. Cache residency is per-model-variant + region by default.

Can you confirm:
1) Will your pilot rely on consistent client-side prefixes (same system + few-shot examples) or will prompts vary a lot?
2) Any procurement constraints around credits for the onboarding month?

I've attached the latest ratecard and a sample SOW draft that includes a proposed $5k pilot credit to offset initial cold-starts. If you want, I can convert that into a short-term commitment quote so procurement can route it faster.

Thanks,
Ben

Alyssa / DataStream procurement,

Thanks for the questions — answering inline below and adding concrete examples: 

1) Per-customer appended tokens: these are considered part of the request payload and are included in the cache key if they are identical across requests. In practice: if you append a static 100-token context for Customer A and that exact 100-token blob is present in subsequent requests, the prefix match will be exact and treated as a hit. If any token in that appended context changes, it's a miss.

2) Pricing examples (using Redwood_ratecard_v5.pdf rates included in the attachment):
- Cold request (no prefix hit):  input prompt = 500 tokens, generated = 200 tokens. Billed tokens = 700. Example rate: $0.0008 / token => charge = $0.56.
- Perfect prefix hit (full prompt cached, only generation charged): cached prompt = 500 tokens, generated = 200 tokens. Billed tokens = 200. Charge = $0.16.
- Partial-match scenario: if 80% of the prompt matches (400 tokens) but 100 tokens differ, we consider it a miss and bill full 700 tokens.

Contract language snippet we propose you can copy into SOW/Order Form:

"Prefix residency (\"cache\") hit definition: a cache hit occurs when the incoming request contains an identical prefix to a cached entry on the serving tier for the same model variant and region. When a cache hit is recorded, Redwood will meter and bill only for the response/generated tokens. Partial or fuzzy matches are not considered hits and will be billed as full requests. Cache residency TTL defaults to 24 hours; custom TTLs may be requested and priced separately."

Pilot credit proposal: we can provide a $5,000 onboarding credit applied to token charges within the first 30 days of rollout. If you prefer a small committed package to simplify procurement, we can do a 3-month $50k commit with a 20% usage discount and absorb the onboarding credit into that commit.

Attached: Redwood_ratecard_v5.pdf (line items and per-token rates) and a draft SOW with the above language.

Let me know if that hits what procurement needs and I can produce a formal quote (DocuSign) tied to deal DS-2026-014.

Cheers,
Ben
